scope: Remove six unused externally sourced images; clarify JAXA terms; prepare one replacement without changing the displayed image. Team paper figures excluded at the owner's request.
historyNote: Removed from the current source tree and deployment. Earlier Git commits still contain the files; no Git history was rewritten.

jaxa.currentUse: An external ground-test example illustrating a possible extension of the team's excavation research to lunar regolith. Public, informational research portfolio; image is unchanged, proportionally displayed and credited to JAXA.
confirmedRules: Academic research and school education/learning, including papers and academic presentations, are listed as free uses that do not require an application, subject to conditions.
Some nonprofit uses by public institutions and NPO/NGO bodies are separately listed as free but requiring application. Private use does not include posting to personal websites or social accounts.
The materials service explicitly covers JAXA website images outside the archive. Attribution, image-specific notices, third-party rights and non-endorsement conditions still apply.

JAXA instructs users to contact its archive when the application category is unclear. Permission, when required, is communicated by email after review; review may take approximately five business days.
jaxa.assessment: The current public research-outreach page is not expressly classified by the policy. Research context supports the academic-use category, while the outreach/portfolio purpose overlaps with institution publicity. Do not treat it as confirmed permission-free reuse, and do not equate Courtesy of JAXA with individual authorization.
jaxa.status: Current-use exemption not conclusively confirmed; no individual JAXA permission obtained. Request classification/permission before relying on an exemption.
jaxa.outreach: No inquiry or application has been sent.

replacement.title: NASA Advanced Planetary Excavator (APEX)
replacement.permissionBasis: NASA media guidelines expressly permit educational/informational web-page use of NASA content without explicit permission, with source acknowledgement and without implied endorsement. The source article identifies this as NASA Glenn's APEX facility and shows no separate third-party copyright notice for this photograph.
replacement.visualReview: Real, single backhoe-style arm, bucket and pedestal visible. No recognizable people. Fixed ground-test installation, not a wheeled/tracked rover and not a photograph taken on the Moon.
replacement.suggestedCaption: NASA's Advanced Planetary Excavator (APEX) for lunar-regolith excavation research. Image: NASA / Glenn Research Center.
replacement.status: Prepared as a replacement candidate; not referenced by the live website.
